We were in our mid-30s and in well-established careers, so we could afford to go all out. Top shelf open bar, food all night, paid extra for a longer reception. Instead of opting for more "traditional" seating charts where you stick people with others they don't know (always annoyed me, I loathe small talk), we sat people with their friend groups. We played the Imperial March as we walked out after the ceremony and the Ewok theme as our last song of the night which cracked a lot of people up. We basically made it more of a really elaborate fun 5 hour party with a 30 minute ceremony and a formal dinner thrown in. We just didn't take it so seriously like other weddings we'd been to; we wanted a fun party, and we made it happen. I know everyone is partial to their own wedding, but we still get comments from friends saying that ours was the best wedding they'd attended and they mention highlights.

We definitely splurged but we also budgeted heavily. We had a nice printer, so we bought card stock and made our own invitations, programs, seating cards, and table cards. We scouted a bunch of locations, and our choice had a lot of flowers and arrangements already so we saved a lot of money on flowers. Little things like the invites and the music really made the wedding "us" and set it apart from the more generic weddings we'd been to. Make sure you make your wedding "you" and it'll absolutely be fun :)
